Q1.title: Result trend for one observation type over a date range
Q1.question: Monthly mean and volume for a single LOINC code across a two-year window, split by patient age band — the shape behind every 'is this measure drifting' tile on a clinical dashboard.
Q1.sql: SELECT d.month_year, p.age_band, COUNT_BIG(*) AS results, AVG(f.value_numeric) AS mean_value FROM dw.FactObservation AS f JOIN dw.DimDate AS d ON d.date_key = f.effective_date_key JOIN dw.DimPatient AS p ON p.patient_key = f.patient_key WHERE f.observation_code_key = ( SELECT TOP (1) observation_code_key FROM dw.FactObservation GROUP BY observation_code_key ORDER BY COUNT_BIG(*) DESC) AND f.is_numeric = 1 AND d.full_date >= '2025-01-01' GROUP BY d.month_year, p.age_band;
Q1.sql_after: SELECT d.month_year, p.age_band, COUNT_BIG(*) AS results, AVG(f.value_numeric) AS mean_value FROM dw.FactObservation AS f JOIN dw.DimDate AS d ON d.date_key = f.effective_date_key JOIN dw.DimPatient AS p ON p.patient_key = f.patient_key WHERE f.observation_code_key = ( SELECT TOP (1) observation_code_key FROM dw.FactObservation GROUP BY observation_code_key ORDER BY COUNT_BIG(*) DESC) AND f.is_numeric = 1 AND d.full_date >= '2025-01-01' GROUP BY d.month_year, p.age_band;
Q1.fix_sql: CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_FactObservation_code_date ON dw.FactObservation (observation_code_key, effective_date_key) INCLUDE (patient_key, value_numeric, is_numeric);

Q2.title: Whole-warehouse aggregate across every observation code
Q2.question: Volume, mean and spread for every observation code by fiscal quarter — the extract behind a Power BI import model, which reads the whole fact table rather than a slice of it.
Q2.sql: SELECT c.code, c.code_display, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_quarter, COUNT_BIG(*) AS results, AVG(f.value_numeric) AS mean_value, MIN(f.value_numeric) AS min_value, MAX(f.value_numeric) AS max_value FROM dw.FactObservation AS f JOIN dw.DimObservationCode AS c ON c.observation_code_key = f.observation_code_key JOIN dw.DimDate AS d ON d.date_key = f.effective_date_key WHERE f.is_numeric = 1 GROUP BY c.code, c.code_display, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_quarter;
Q2.sql_after: SELECT c.code, c.code_display, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_quarter, COUNT_BIG(*) AS results, AVG(f.value_numeric) AS mean_value, MIN(f.value_numeric) AS min_value, MAX(f.value_numeric) AS max_value FROM dw.FactObservation AS f JOIN dw.DimObservationCode AS c ON c.observation_code_key = f.observation_code_key JOIN dw.DimDate AS d ON d.date_key = f.effective_date_key WHERE f.is_numeric = 1 GROUP BY c.code, c.code_display, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_quarter;
Q2.fix_sql: CREATE NONCLUSTERED COLUMNSTORE INDEX NCCI_FactObservation ON dw.FactObservation (observation_code_key, effective_date_key, patient_key, value_numeric, is_numeric);

Q3.title: Reference resolution across the whole raw table
Q3.question: The shape of every shredding statement: pull a FHIR reference out of a million JSON documents and turn it into a local key. Not a reporting query — the load itself, which is where this warehouse spends most of its time. The fix here is a rewrite rather than an index, and it is the largest single change in the repository.
Q3.sql: SELECT COUNT_BIG(*) AS resolved FROM raw.fhir_resource AS r WHERE r.resource_type = 'Observation' AND dbo.fn_reference_id_multi_statement( JSON_VALUE(r.payload, '$.subject.reference')) IS NOT NULL;
Q3.sql_after: SELECT COUNT_BIG(*) AS resolved FROM raw.fhir_resource AS r CROSS APPLY norm.tvf_reference_id( JSON_VALUE(r.payload, '$.subject.reference')) AS subj WHERE r.resource_type = 'Observation' AND subj.resource_id IS NOT NULL;
Q3.fix: replace the scalar UDF with an inline table-valued function
